newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 18.

text.p: Following are the highlight sof stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton has given his backing to Ireland's view that Sinn Fein should be rapidly admitted to peace talks if the Irish Republican Army calls a new ceasefire.
- New legislation increasing funding for the offices of party leaders to 1.5 million punts a year from 600,000 is to be rushed through parliament on Wednesday.
- The Blood Transfusion Service Board and Department of Health are discussing how to implement an optional HIV testing programme for people who received possibly infected blood between 1981 and 1985.
- The next Budget is not expected to include any reduction in the top rate of income tax, according to sources close to the national pay talks.
- Eastman Kodak is expected to announce a new plant in Limerick which will create 400 jobs.
- The Irish pound fell decisively below parity against sterling on Tuesday as the central bank withdrew the support it had been giving the currency at this level.
- This year's housing boom has pushed mortgage borrowing above two billion punts for the first time.
- Communications minister Alan Dukes has placed a five-year cap on a range of telephone charges and predicted overall prices would fall by a third in that time.
